An unprecedented joint letter dispenses with diplomatic language by accusing Israel of ethnic cleansing and warning that the world no longer sees Israel as a genuine democracy.

Uphold the decisions of the international court of justice and the international criminal court.

Suspend the EU-Israel association agreement and the UK-Israel trade and partnership agreement for breach of human rights provisions.

Warn potential bidders for the “red line” E1 settlement or other settlement financing/construction that their interests in and with the UK and France will suffer.

Make it an offence for British and French citizens to buy property on stolen Palestinian land and remove charitable status from “charities” funding settlements.

events.title: The return of the caspian tiger: how a species feared extinct has come back to Kazakhstan
events.summary:
The wild capture and release of a female big cat into a nature reserve is the first step towards reintroducing a population that hasn’t been seen for 70 years

On 31 July, “Umit” – which means hope in Kazakh – was released into a nature reserve on the edge of Lake Balkhash after more than a decade of careful planning to return the caspian tiger to the region. With this release, Kazakhstan became the first country to restore its tiger range after they had been thought extinct, with the last reliable sighting in the country recorded more than 70 years ago.

Umit – a wild-caught female tiger transported from the Russian far east – will be joined by more big cats in the coming years, with plans to establish a self-sustaining population of about 50. A wild-caught male flown from Russia is still being monitored by authorities and will be released when he is judged fit to survive alone. Two wild tiger cubs are also being reared on the reserve in special enclosures, with as little human contact as possible, and are likely to be released into the marshlands next year, to feast on boar, deer and kulans, a type of wild donkey.

events.title: Bus crash in Hungary kills at least 12
events.summary: Police say they have arrested the driver of a bus that crashed in Hungary, killing at least 12 people. The bus was carrying Polish pilgrims, media report.

events.title: Will North Korean forces bolster Russia's Ukraine war?
events.summary: Intelligence agencies report that North Korea could send up to 50,000 troops to support Russia in its war on Ukraine, though experts doubt this will fundamentally shift the military balance in Moscow’s favor.

events.title: How Germany supports recovery of Berlin Pride attack victims
events.summary: After a terrorist attack, public attention tends to focus primarily on the perpetrator. But what about the victims? What support can they expect? And what lies ahead for them?

events.title: In Germany, record heat meets climate action fatigue
events.summary: Climate action does not seem to be a priority for the German government — despite record temperatures, heat-related deaths and drought. Why aren't more people taking to the streets in protest?

events.title: Afghan allies still waiting for the safety Germany promised
events.summary: After the Taliban retook power on August 15, 2021, Berlin promised to bring Afghan staff to Germany. But people are still waiting to leave in Pakistan and Afghanistan.

events.title: Germany: Evacuated villagers return after Eifel wildfire eases
events.summary: Most residents evacuated from the village of Gey have returned home after firefighters brought a major wildfire in Germany's Eifel region largely under control. DW has more.

events.title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?
events.summary: The Russian House stands in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it's being used to spread propaganda for Putin's Russia. Now, French authorities have said it is being used by the Kremlin for espionage.

events.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
events.summary: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.

events.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
events.summary: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

events.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
events.summary: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.

events.title: How Germany's drone defense fails
events.summary: Drone defense is a priority for the German government. The latest dramatic incident involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport shows there are still substantial shortcomings.

events.title: Germany news: Far-right leader backs left-wing populist
events.summary: The leader of the far-right AfD in Thuringia, Björn Höcke, has offered to back populist Sahra Wagenknecht as state premier. And heat-related deaths this year are now numbered at some 12,500. DW has more.

events.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?
events.summary: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

events.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
events.summary: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

events.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
events.summary: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

events.title: Unconstitutional? German intelligence to receive more powers
events.summary: German intelligence agencies have been calling for more powers in the fight against cyberattacks, terrorism and extremism. Now the government has given the go. Critics warn that red lines are being crossed.

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
events.summary: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.

events.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
events.summary: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
events.summary: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
events.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

events.title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
events.summary: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

events.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
events.summary: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.

events.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
events.summary: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.

events.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
events.summary: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.

events.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
events.summary: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

events.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
events.summary: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

events.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
events.summary: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

events.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
events.summary: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.

events.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
events.summary: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

events.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football
events.summary: Gianni Infantino is staying on as FIFA president despite growing pressure to step down. So who is football's most powerful man, why did UEFA and others turn against him, and how did he reassert his authority?

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
events.summary: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.

events.title: The hidden problem with small modular nuclear reactors
events.summary: Mini nuclear reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep
events.summary: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.

events.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
events.summary: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: More cancer-prone? Why younger generations may be at risk
events.summary: Researchers are observing certain age-related types of cancer more frequently in younger people. A new study suggests this could be because younger generations are aging faster than their parents or grandparents.

events.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'
events.summary: Flexing achievements? Cringe. Expressing genuine emotions? Cringe. You want to look away, but you can’t. Cringe. It's so addictive, people have built social media careers by monetizing other people's worst moments.

events.title: What happens next for Infantino and FIFA?
events.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under pressure after the failure of his plan to create a commercial subsidiary for the World Cup. But will he be ousted? And what is needed for that to happen?

events.title: The economic toll of Spain's wildfires
events.summary: Devastating wildfires are ravaging Spain's tourism, economy and nature. Could the country have done more to prevent them?

events.title: Germany: As temperatures rise, so does climate skepticism
events.summary: Some 98% of active climate scientists say climate change is happening, and is man-made. Nonetheless, a new study shows the number of climate-change skeptics in Germany has increased. Why is that?

events.title: More women die in heatwaves, but biology 'isn't main cause'
events.summary: In country after country, more women are dying from the heat than men. But researchers say biology isn't the main reason. Age, working conditions, and unequal access to rest may drive the gap.

events.title: What's really causing Europe's wildfires
events.summary: From Greece to France, Europe is burning. But what's the real reason for the historic blazes ripping through the continent and why are they getting harder to stop?

events.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
events.summary: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

events.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
events.summary: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominate. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

events.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
events.summary: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

events.title: FIFA plans: Infantino under pressure as senior advisor quits
events.summary: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

events.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights
events.summary: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

events.title: BMW to Volkswagen: How deep is Germany's auto industry cull?
events.summary: BMW joins VW, Porsche and Mercedes-Benz in cutting thousands of jobs, as Chinese rivals erode their market share. DW recaps the major reforms German automakers are pursuing to safeguard their future.

events.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell-off
events.summary: Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may be ready to oppose Infantino's re-election.

events.title: 'Rienzi': Why this Wagner opera is so relevant today
events.summary: The opera sparked controversy long before its Bayreuth Festival premiere, and the debate hasn't died down since it came to the stage. Now, another controversy surrounds the new AI-generated Ring cycle.

events.title: K-pop's BTS opt out of new Asian music Grammy consideration
events.summary: The K-pop sensation BTS, snubbed when nominated for Grammys in the past, say they're not interested in winning a new Asian music category.

events.title: World Cup sell-off: Has FIFA finally gone too far?
events.summary: A new FIFA proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup has been met with fury in the football world. Under Gianni Infantino’s presidency, FIFA has become increasingly profit-driven, but is this too much?

events.title: Bayreuth Festival opens with celebration and commemoration
events.summary: To mark its 150th anniversary, the Bayreuth Festival remembers victims of the Holocaust — and confronts its founder's antisemitism.

events.title: How two wars and El Nino could fuel world hunger
events.summary: The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East haven't yet crippled global food supplies. Add a powerful weather pattern like El Nino, however, and the risks multiply.

events.title: Germany: How weather extremes impact local agriculture
events.summary: Heat, drought, heavy rain and late frosts are taking a toll on German farmers. They increasingly respond with adapted varieties, new crops, modern breeding techniques and modified farming methods.

events.title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake
events.summary: FIFA has announced plans to form a commercial subsidiary and to sell a non-controlling interest to private investors. It needs approval from member associations, but is claiming that it will benefit them financially.

events.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?
events.summary: As the Autobahn buckles under heat waves, Germany is still paving roads for a past climate. Engineers know how to fix that — so what's the holdup?

events.title: 'Loneliness influencers': Being alone brings in the clicks
events.summary: No friends, no dating, no problem? Many influencers are presenting social isolation as a lifestyle. But experts warn of the consequences.

events.title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?
events.summary: Though Iran continues to attack vessels as leverage in its war with the United States, data show that several shippers continue to transit the waterway.

events.title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
events.summary: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

events.title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics
events.summary: In a strongly worded open statement, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit out at those he says were too "consumed by hate and criticism" to enjoy the tournament. Infantino brushed off a number of corruption concerns.

events.title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
events.summary: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

events.title: MBS in the City of Light: In a world of realpolitik, does West value economic interests over values?
events.summary: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Susanne Koelbl, Der Spiegel's award-winning foreign correspondent. According to Koelbl,, Emmanuel Macron’s decision to welcome Mohammed bin Salman at the Élysée reflects realpolitik in its purest form: 'Saudi Arabia had become too important for energy, regional security, investment and diplomacy in the Middle East to be permanently isolated. So Macron wanted to establish France as an independent, balanced power between the Mediterranean and the Gulf."

events.title: Ceasefire verification mission deploys to eastern DR Congo
events.summary: A ceasefire verification mission comprised of representatives from DR Congo's government, the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 rebel group, and observers from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) member nations arrived in South Kivu on Monday. The deployment came a day after the DRC and AFC/M23 agreed on a Switzerland-mediated roadmap for peace talks.

events.title: Ukraine celebrates Independence Day amid war's latest escalation
events.summary: Ukraine wants ​peace but will not just give in to Russia at any price, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a defiant speech on Monday as foreign leaders gathered in Kyiv to mark its Independence Day celebrations.

events.title: ‘We don’t need Canada’: Trump threatens to double auto tariffs after trade talks collapse
events.summary: US tariffs ​on all Canadian cars and trucks, automotive parts and steel will be increased to 50% starting January 1, 2027, President Donald Trump said Monday, adding that the US does not “need” Canada after the collapse of trade talks. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said his administration had been “patient” during negotiations, but Canada would not do a deal “at any price”.

events.title: With 'rare' Paris talks, France hopes to cash in on Saudi investment programme
events.summary: Saudi's crown prince Mohammed bin Salman is in Paris to meet France's President Emmanuel Macron. The two leaders are to hold talks on a variety of topics, but first and foremost about the situation in the Middle East. For France, this is a chance to benefit from Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 investment plan. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali is at the Elysée Palace and tells us more.

events.title: What could new US sanctions on Iran entail?
events.summary: The US says it is preparing to announce new sanctions on Iran. It's been billed an economic D-day and is expected to add further pressure on the country's economy that's already been battered from previous sanctions and a US naval blockade. The renewed economic pressure would not be the first time the US has used economic tools at its disposal to corner Iran. But what could the new measures likely entail?

events.title: France's left fractures further as MEP launches presidential bid
events.summary: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann announced his candidacy for France's presidential election next year, joining a crowded field of far-right figures, centrists and fellow left-wingers. Hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon is planning to stand while Greens leader Marine Tondelier is campaigning while pregnant, socialist Party (PS) leader Olivier Faure and even possibly ex-president Francois Hollande are also mulling runs.

events.title: Ukraine showing ‘remarkable innovation’: Kyiv ‘holding front line’ while striking Russia’s economy
events.summary: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Samantha de Bendern, Associate Fellow at Chatham House. Europe is taking increasingly consequential steps to support Ukraine, but de Bendern warns that they remain insufficient to address the country's fundamental vulnerability. Are Ukraine's allies prepared to actively help protect Ukrainian airspace? That debate reaches back to the earliest weeks of the full-scale invasion: even after President Biden warned in 2022 of an imminent Russian attack, Kyiv's allies ruled out enforcing a no-fly zone, fearing that direct NATO engagement could escalate into a wider war with Moscow.

events.title: Mideast live: Trump claims Iran is ‘completely collapsing’ as US readies new sanctions
events.summary: President Donald Trump on Monday said Iran is "completely collapsing" in a message posted on social media just hours before the US was set to announce details of new sanctions against Tehran. Iran’s foreign ministry has warned that Tehran will respond harshly to expanded sanctions, including measures against countries cooperating with Washington. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

events.title: Guinea searches for survivors after landfill landslides kill 30
events.summary: In Guinea, a landslide at a garbage dump outside the capital Conakry has claimed the lives of at least 30 people. The government of the West African country says it has mobilised significant resources to try and find survivors that may still be trapped under massive piles of waste. Less than a week ago, that same government had announced plans to close the Dar-es-Salam landfill due to dangerous conditions there.

events.title: US sanctions 'unlikely to get Tehran to bow down' despite effect on population
events.summary: Iran has warned that Tehran would respond harshly to expanded U.S. sanctions, including measures against countries it sees as cooperating with Washington. The expanded sanctions come after weeks of impasse. The United States has not dislodged Iran’s grip on the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil passed before the war started nearly six months ago. Now, Washington is hoping the extra sanctions will bring change. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah tells us about the atmosphere in Iran, from Tehran.

events.title: Humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m world record
events.summary: Robots exceeded human records at the World Robot Games over the weekend in Beijing's Olympic speed skating arena as China showcased its dominance in the industry. Dozens of humanoids and their human operators competed in events from athletics and boxing to football and martial arts.

events.title: Europe ramps up support to Ukraine as its US-dependent air defence runs low
events.summary: European leaders are meeting Kyiv as Ukraine holds celebrations for its 35th Independence Day. The so-called Coalition of the Willing is set to hold talks regarding support to the country, four-and-a-half years after the Russian invasion started, with the European Union having announced it was releasing over six billion euros in aid. But US support to Kyiv regarding critical air defence is still missing. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

events.title: Volkswagen warns Germany's car-making industry is in jeopardy
events.summary: The CEO of the German car-making group Volkswagen is warning that the situation at the company is "more than critical". Oliver Blume is saying that ahead of meetings with the car giant's staff. He says Volkswagen and the rest of Germany's car industry are facing "the biggest upheaval in their history" due to global headwinds and Chinese competition.

events.title: 'Scared to death': Over 40,000 people evacuated as Nevada's Hawk fire spreads
events.summary: An additional 45,000 people have been placed under evacuation warnings in the northwestern US state of Nevada. This comes as the fast moving Hawk fire threatens the city of Reno. According to officials the fire was "human caused", but they have not detailed if it was set intentionally. Eight hundred firefighters have been mobilized to bring the blazes under control. Unpredictable winds have complicated the effort, and so far there's been zero percent containment.

events.title: France and Saudi Arabia hold talks ranging from Middle East to esports
events.summary: Mohammed bin Salman has arrived in Paris for a two-day official visit with French President Emmanuel Macron. Talks are expected to include the war in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as new energy routes to bypass the Strait. The two made an appearance at the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup, held for the first time outside of Saudi Arabia but largely funded by Riyadh.

events.title: War-torn Ukraine celebrates resilience on anniversary of its independence
events.summary: August 24 marks the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence, and it also marks four and a half years of conflict with Russia. As European leaders meet in Kyiv, the Coalition of the Willing is set to chair a meeting with Volodymr Zelensky to discuss ways to bolster support for Ukraine, which is facing an escalating bombing campaign from Moscow.

events.title: Iran calls France's decision to expel two Iranian diplomats 'illegal'
events.summary: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday said France's decision to expel two of its diplomats was “illegal”. France's move came in retaliation for Tehran's decision not to allow two French diplomats to return to its territory.

events.title: Strategic talks in Paris show France and Saudi Arabia 'need each other too much'
events.summary: The Saudi crown prince and French President Emmanuel Macron are to chair on August 24 the first meeting of the Saudi-French strategic partnership council, and a number of agreements arer expected to be signed. Among them are a new Dragon-Ball themed amusement park deal in the Paris region and the sale of French military equipment to the kingdom. FRANCE 24's Philip Turle tells us more on what to know about the talks.

events.title: Despite ceasefire, Israeli strikes still kill in Gaza and the West Bank
events.summary: Despite a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025, violence continues in Gaza. On August 23, Israeli strikes left several people dead in the enclave, and a young boy was killed by the Israeli military in the West Bank, according to local authorities.  Since the announcement of the truce, more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has reported the launch of drones, balloons and kites towards its territory.

events.title: European leaders rally in Kyiv to celebrate Ukraine's Independence Day
events.summary: European leaders joined President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on August 24 for official celebrations marking Ukraine’s Independence Day as Russia pushes on with its four-year-old invasion of the country. Among the guests is new UK prime minister Andy Burnham, his first overseas trip since taking office in July. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze tells us more from Kyiv.

events.title: Ligue 1: Ferran Torres saves Paris Saint-Germain against Rennes
events.summary: Paris Saint-Germain snatched a draw away at Rennes (2-2) on the opening day of Ligue 1. Ferran Torres, Paris’s new signing, came on after the break and saved the day for PSG.

events.title: Live: Zelensky calls on allies to cover €27 billion gap for Ukraine’s air defence needs
events.summary: President Volodymyr ​Zelensky on Monday urged Ukraine's ​allies to help ​cover a funding gap of €27 billion for ​its air defence needs ​in 2026. Ukraine is hosting a meeting of its key European backers in Kyiv as the country marks its 35th Independence Day. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

events.title: Landslide kills 30 after mound of waste collapses at landfill site
events.summary: A landslide at a waste site in Guinea has killed 30 people after a mound of rubbish collapsed on to nearby homes.

events.title: Police presence and 'deep sadness' at funeral for one of five teens killed in Ireland head-on collision
events.summary: A funeral mass has been held for one of the teenagers killed in a head-on collision in County Kildare last week - with a heavy police presence at Carlow for the event.

events.title: Maradona 'Hand of God' football sells for £2.5m
events.summary: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his "Hand of God" goal against England in 1986 has been sold at auction for £2.5m.

events.title: Cricket legends urge Pakistan to provide 'proper medical care' for Imran Khan
events.summary: Former cricket captains - including Sir Alastair Cook and Mike Atherton - have urged Pakistan to ensure jailed former prime minister Imran Khan receives "humane treatment and proper medical care".

events.title: Dutch broadcaster to boycott Eurovision 2027
events.summary: Dutch broadcaster AvroTros will boycott next year's Eurovision Song Contest, in protest at Israel's participation in the competition amid the war in Gaza.

events.title: Health of Norway's King Harald deteriorated at the weekend, say royal officials
events.summary: Norway's King Harald is in a stable condition in hospital after his health deteriorated at the weekend, royal officials have said.

events.title: Nordic FAs lose confidence in FIFA chief Gianni Infantino
events.summary: The six Nordic football associations have announced they have lost confidence in Gianni Infantino - intensifying pressure on the FIFA president.

events.title: Shein targets $27bn valuation in stock market debut
events.summary: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein is to make its stock market debut targeting a valuation almost a quarter of the $100bn it was worth four years ago.

events.title: Marathon organisers admit 'unfortunate' medals error
events.summary: In a week, up to 40,000 runners will take part in Sydney's Marathon, but a mix-up means they will be handed medals decorated with a German stadium.

events.title: 'America has changed': Canada to match Trump's tariffs 'dollar for dollar' after trade talks collapse
events.summary: The United States has imposed a 50% tariff on $20bn (£14.6bn) worth of goods from Canada, which has vowed to retaliate against its historic ally.

events.title: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott convicted of sexually abusing 2 children
events.summary: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been convicted of sexually abusing two primary school children in Scotland

events.title: Denmark's prime minister blasts beauty advice from plastic surgeon on Instagram
events.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has expressed frustration over unsolicited beauty advice

events.summary: Two United Nations peacekeepers have been killed in an ambush in South Sudan

events.title: Prince Harry to leave board of African Parks conservation nonprofit
events.summary: Prince Harry is stepping down as a trustee of African Parks, a nonprofit managing protected areas in 13 countries

events.title: The UK will help Ukraine make long-range missiles by sharing classified tech information
events.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announces the U.K. will help Ukraine make its own long-range missiles

events.title: Ukraine amputee veterans celebrate independence day with grueling endurance challenge
events.summary: Military amputees and veterans in Ukraine marked Independence Day by completing Iron Week, a grueling seven-day endurance event covering more than 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) across the country

events.title: Kazakhstan's pro-government party wins parliamentary election
events.summary: Officials say Kazakhstan’s pro-government Adilet Oarty won a landslide victory in the Central Asian country’s parliamentary elections

events.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak records one of its highest weekly death tolls yet
events.summary: More than 300 people have died of Ebola in eastern Congo in the past week, according to government data

events.title: South African police arrest 4 in the killing of former champion boxer Zolani Tete
events.summary: South African police have arrested four suspects in the killing of former world champion boxer Zolani Tete

events.title: Eastern Libya executes 10 convicted on terrorism charges, sparking rights outcry
events.summary: Authorities in eastern Libya have executed 10 people after military courts convicted them on terrorism-related charges

events.title: Hungarian air force Gripen jet crashes, pilot ejects safely, prime minister says
events.summary: A Hungarian military pilot ejected to safety after a fighter jet crashed near the city of Szolnok, Prime Minister Péter Magyar said

events.title: Iran's rial currency hits new record low as US prepares to announce more sanctions
events.summary: Iran’s currency has hit a record low as Washington prepares to announce new sanctions

events.title: Cricket captains from around the world renew appeal for medical treatment of Imran Khan
events.summary: Famous cricketers from around the world have renewed their appeal for the medical treatment of former star player turned politician Imran Khan in a letter to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif

events.summary: European leaders have joined President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv for the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s Independence Day

events.title: The health of Norway's King Harald deteriorates over the weekend
events.summary: King Harald of Norway's health has deteriorated, according to the royal palace

events.title: Japanese lawmakers travel to Beijing, seeking to mend ties after fallout
events.summary: Lawmakers from Japan have traveled to Beijing to meet with Chinese officials in the first visit since tensions rose after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's comment on Taiwan angered China

events.title: What to know about Iceland's vote on whether to restart talks to join the EU
events.summary: Icelanders are voting Saturday on whether to restart talks about joining the European Union

events.title: Chinese workers worry over being replaced as they adapt to the growing impact of AI
events.summary: Artificial intelligence is beginning to reshape China's job market, supported by state policies that some economists believe might undermine the overall strength of its economy

events.title: Mexican governor indicted by the US seeks leave again after contentious return to office
